title: Foundations
blurb: Before any of it could be applied, a machine had to be able to set its own weights — and then to do it through more than one layer.

courses.title: Assigning blame to a hidden unit
courses.blurb: A machine that could not learn XOR, and the chain rule that made depth trainable at all.

courses.title: The energy-based detour
courses.blurb: For twenty years the way to train a deep net was to pretrain it one layer at a time. AlexNet ended that, but the ideas did not go away.

courses.title: Making the optimiser cooperate
courses.blurb: Backpropagation gives a gradient. Everything after is about the step you take with it.

title: Computer vision
blurb: The convolutional architecture was settled in 1980. Everything since is about getting gradients through more of it, and then about whether convolution was needed at all.

courses.title: Making networks deep enough to matter
courses.blurb: Each step is a reason the previous stack stopped training, and what somebody did about it.

courses.title: The same accuracy on a phone
courses.blurb: Separable convolutions, then a search over architectures, then a rule for scaling one.

courses.title: From classifying to locating
courses.blurb: Region proposals, then sharing the convolutions, then removing the hand-built post-processing entirely.

courses.title: Labelling every pixel
courses.blurb: Classification throws away where. Segmentation is the line of work that puts it back.

courses.title: An architecture crosses domains
courses.blurb: Attention was built for translation. Cutting an image into patches let the same block read pictures.

title: Language and sequence
blurb: A recurrent net reads one word at a time and forgets. Removing the recurrence is what let these models scale with the hardware.

courses.title: The road to the Transformer
courses.blurb: Sixty years from a machine that could not learn XOR to one that reads a sentence in a single parallel step.

courses.title: Pre-train once, use everywhere
courses.blurb: Transfer stopped meaning word vectors and started meaning the whole model.

courses.title: Teaching a model what was wanted
courses.blurb: Predicting the next token is not the same as being useful — and the last step does it without a reward model at all.

courses.title: The open-weight line
courses.blurb: The same recipe, trained longer on more tokens, and released so anyone could build on it.

title: Generative models
blurb: Three answers to one question — compress and decode, fool a critic, or reverse a noising process — and the argument between them.

courses.title: Compress, then sample
courses.blurb: An autoencoder only reconstructs. Making its middle a distribution is what turns it into a generator.

courses.title: Training against a critic
courses.blurb: Sharp images and an optimisation that would not sit still. Six years of trying to stabilise it.

courses.title: How diffusion overtook GANs
courses.blurb: Score matching gave a likelihood and a slow sampler. The line that won made it fast.

courses.title: Keeping the likelihood exact
courses.blurb: Invertible maps with a tractable Jacobian, all the way to a continuous-time version of the same idea.

title: Reinforcement learning
blurb: Thirty years on games, and then the same policy-gradient machinery turned out to be how a language model is taught to follow instructions.

courses.title: From a table to a network
courses.blurb: Dynamic programming needs the whole model. Everything here is about not having it.

courses.title: Optimising the policy directly
courses.blurb: High-variance gradients, then a trust region, then the clipped objective that made it practical.

courses.title: Learning the reward instead
courses.blurb: When the reward is the thing you cannot write down, infer it from someone doing the task.

title: Multimodal
blurb: Captioning taught a network to describe an image. Contrastive pretraining put images and sentences in the same coordinates, which is what made everything since possible.

courses.title: Describing what is in the picture
courses.blurb: A vision encoder and a language decoder, joined first by a vector and then by attention.

courses.title: One space for both
courses.blurb: Once images and text share coordinates, a language model can be handed an image and simply carry on.
